## Verdict

The repo is in decent shape; the failure is concentrated in three places, and most of the proposed work is additive. The single most important structural finding before you write any contextual code:

**`flat_exhaustive` is not exhaustive.** `flat_search` (`src/tkh_abstraction/search_v2.py:83`) ranks only nodes whose type is in `route['types']`, but `entity_metrics` (`src/tkh_abstraction/evaluation/retrieval_v2.py:20`) computes recall over gold nodes resolved by `resolve_target` across `ENTITY_TYPES | {claim}` (`target_mapping.py:42`). A gold node typed `problem`, `metric`, `future_topic`, or `article` under the `methods` route is structurally unreachable — recall 0 is then guaranteed by construction, not by ranking. The Phase-0 audit must carry `eligible_after_type_routing` as a first-class field, and the fix is PART F (routing becomes a prior, candidate pool becomes all entity types), not a better retriever.

---

## 1. Substantive methodological risks

**R-a. Query/document asymmetry is an un-attributed confound.** `node_texts` emits `"method: MACE"` (`semantics.py:41`) and questions are encoded raw (`v2_pipeline.py:45`). BGE-small-en-v1.5 is an asymmetric retriever trained with a query-side instruction prefix; you are currently using it symmetrically, 3-token docs against 30-word queries. Adding the prefix is benchmark-independent and needs no new model — but it will move *every* v2 number. Give it its own ablation row (**R0b = flat_surface + prefixed query**) between R0 and R1. If you fold it into R1 you can no longer claim the gain came from graph context.

**R-b. Multi-field scoring silently redefines the cost unit.** Today 1 entity = 1 dot product. With per-field vectors an entity costs 10–50 dot products. If contextual flat keeps charging 1/entity while the hierarchy charges `1 + prototypes` per unit, the entire quality/cost plot (`report_v2.py:110`) becomes uninterpretable and PART P's conclusion is predetermined. Fix the unit *before* R1 (see §3).

**R-c. Grouping moves the denominator, so the R1→R2 delta is not clean.** Two independent effects fire at once: (i) if two gold nodes merge into one group, `R` shrinks and Recall@k rises with zero retrieval improvement; (ii) top-k becomes k *groups* rather than k *nodes*, which is strictly more information at nominally the same k. Guard: build the group partition once, query-independently, before any ablation; map gold to groups using that same partition in **both** R1 and R2 so denominators are byte-identical; assert equality in code; and record `nodes_covered_by_topk_groups` so the slot-budget effect is visible.

**R-d. Composites and evidence-only targets will quietly distort every conditional metric.** `EVIDENCE_BACKED` targets have no node to retrieve — if they sit in the Recall@k denominator, every ablation row is capped by a constant and the R0–R5 deltas compress. If you drop them, you violate PART M. They need separate named denominators (§4), not a judgment call per metric.

**R-e. Containment aliasing is unsafe and internally inconsistent.** `resolve_target` (`target_mapping.py:44-46`) admits `cited_work` to the exact set but excludes it from the containment set, and accepts bare `contains_name` with no identifier-token floor — so a 3-char acronym matches any node whose name contains it (the `test_ambiguous_alias_is_not_truth` case only survives because *two* candidates collide). A2 requires meaningful identifier evidence. Use a **graph-derived** generic-head-noun filter (tokens above a fixed document-frequency percentile over node surface forms) rather than any written list; that keeps it benchmark-independent and is a structural constant, not a tuned threshold.

**R-f. Relation direction does not exist in the data.** Hyperedges carry `members` as an ordered list with no `roles`/`head` keys (verified by grep). Direction can only be inferred from the `members[0]`-is-subject convention plus type signature. Treat that as a stated assumption and *measure* it — e.g. the fraction of `evaluated_on` edges where `members[0].type == 'method'` and the rest are dataset/metric — and emit the fraction into the artifact. If it is low, fall back to type-signature role assignment.

**R-g. Article-provenance context is a firehose and actively harms Type-A discrimination.** `meth_00030` carries 6 articles; the existing `entity_article_claim` path (`search_v2.py:106-109`) attaches every claim sharing any article. For methods co-occurring in one survey, that makes MACE's context and NequIP's context nearly identical — exactly the wrong failure mode for a multi-answer method question. Keep direct-hyperedge claims as the primary `claim` field and article-shared claims as a **separate, lower-weight field** exposed as its own ablation.

**R-h. Broad hyperedges.** A real `extends` edge in the data has 8 method members. Naive co-member expansion injects 7 competitor names into each method's representation. Enforce `context_max_arity`: above it, contribute relation-type text only (or `members[0]`↔member pairs), never the full co-member name list — and never into name-like fields.

**R-i. Cost accounting already favours flat on Type-B.** `v2_pipeline.py:69` passes `result['leaf_scores']` as `known_scores`; flat has scores for every eligible node (claims free), the hierarchy has scores for only the handful of leaves it reached. `report_v2.py:22` then prints a single `total_comparisons`. Principled but apples-to-oranges. Split permanently into `entity_comparisons`, `claim_comparisons_new`, `claim_comparisons_reused`; never headline a single total.

**R-j. Snapshot strips fields you may want.** `snapshots.py:11` pops `last_seen_year`, and pops `year`/`origin_year` when `> cutoff`. Temporal scoring must use `first_seen_year` (always present) and treat `year`/`origin_year` as optional — `.get`, not `[]`.

**R-k. `verify_reuse` fragility.** `v2_pipeline.py:17-27` hashes everything in `manifest['core_sources']` and `manifest['artifact_sha256']`. Check whether that manifest lists any `src/**` paths *before* adding modules; if it does, adding a file breaks baseline reuse. (`protocol.code_hashes` at `v2_pipeline.py:34` merely records, so that one is safe.)

---

## 2. Bounded plan — new modules, existing files mostly untouched

To preserve v1/v2 results exactly, **do not edit** `target_mapping.py`, `search_v2.py`, `evaluation/retrieval_v2.py`, or `report_v2.py`. The v2 path must keep producing identical artifacts.

| File | Action |
|---|---|
| `src/tkh_abstraction/resolution.py` | **new** — `TargetResolution`, `ResolutionType` enum, conservative normalizer, `resolve_target(label, graph)`, composite splitter, evidence-backed detection, `map_benchmark_v3`, `resolution_summary` |
| `src/tkh_abstraction/entity_groups.py` | **new** — `EntityGroup`, `build_entity_groups(nodes)`; query-independent, identical-normalized-name + certified-alias only |
| `src/tkh_abstraction/context.py` | **new** — `NodeRetrievalRepresentation`, relation-aware field extraction with caps, arity guard, `members[0]` role inference + its validation report |
| `src/tkh_abstraction/query_analysis.py` | **new** — `analyze_question → QueryIntent`, deterministic extractive views (E2) |
| `src/tkh_abstraction/scoring.py` | **new** — field aggregation (max / mean-top-m, configurable), soft type priors, temporal score, score decomposition |
| `src/tkh_abstraction/search_context.py` | **new** — `flat_context_search`, `ContextSearchIndex` (R7/R8) returning the **same result dict keys** as `search_v2` (test S23) |
| `src/tkh_abstraction/evaluation/retrieval_v3.py` | **new** — outcome classification, named denominators, Hit/Recall/Precision@k, MRR, R-Prec, Recall@R, three aggregations |
| `src/tkh_abstraction/semantics.py` | **edit, additive** — `query_texts()` with the BGE instruction prefix; leave `node_texts` byte-identical |
| `src/tkh_abstraction/cli.py` | **edit** — `evaluate-context` command + PART W flags |
| `configs/contextual.yaml` | **new** — do not touch `evaluation_v2.yaml`; its protocol is frozen |
| `scripts/audit_gold_candidates.py`, `scripts/run_ablations.py` | **new** |
| `src/tkh_abstraction/report_v3.py` | **new** — appends a section; `report_v2.generate_report` untouched |

**Key efficiency lever:** a method's claim-field vectors are simply the rows of the already-computed `X` for its claim neighbors. Build field vectors by *gathering* from `X`, not by re-encoding. That makes the entire contextual index cost ~0 extra encoder calls and keeps `.cache/embeddings` valid. Only the query prefix (`query_texts`) requires new encodes.

**Ordering.** A: baseline + `gold_candidate_audit.json` (Codex, in flight) — add `eligible_after_type_routing`. B: resolution + `target_resolution.json` + tests S1–S9. C: grouping, freeze the gold group partition, tests S10/S11/S24. D: context + scoring; run R0, **R0b**, R1. **E: hard checkpoint — publish R0/R0b/R1 before writing any further code.** F: R2→R5 one at a time. G: R7/R8 only if the checkpoint shows material recall.

---

## 3. Fixed field and cost accounting (propose freezing this before R1)

- **Unit, unchanged:** one dot product of a query vector with one stored unit vector = 1 charged comparison.
- **Fixed field schema with hard, query-independent caps** (config, not tuned): `name` 1, `article` ≤2, `claim_direct` ≤4, `claim_article` ≤4, `task` ≤3, `problem` ≤2, `technique` ≤3, `component` ≤3, `dataset` ≤3 → ≤25 vectors/entity.
- **Deterministic within-cap selection:** order by `(relation arity asc, neighbor node id asc)`. Never by query similarity — that is unpaid ranking, the exact trap `retrieval.py:28` already guards against.
- **Report three columns, never one:** `entities_scored`, `vectors_scored`, `query_views`. With the name field alone, `vectors_scored == entities_scored` and R0 cost reduces exactly to today's number, so R0↔R1 cost stays comparable.
- **Multi-query:** total charge multiplies by `query_views`; log it so R4's cost is visible rather than hidden.
- **Hierarchy units use the identical field schema** (per-field centroid over eligible members), so a unit charge = number of non-empty fields (+ prototypes) and is the same kind of object as a leaf charge.
- **Offline excluded and timed separately** via the existing `index_seconds` (`v2_pipeline.py:44`).
- Claim/evidence cost split into `claim_comparisons_new` / `claim_comparisons_reused` (R-i).

---

## 4. Fixed evaluation denominators (emit the definition string next to every metric)

Each (question, target) instance gets exactly one resolution type and exactly one PART-M outcome.

- `D_all` — all 63 expected instances. Denominator for `end_to_end_recall`. **Never shrinks, in any run.**
- `D_representable` — EXACT + ALIAS + COMPOSITE + EVIDENCE_BACKED.
- `D_node_bearing` — EXACT + ALIAS + COMPOSITE whose components are all node-bearing. Denominator for `candidate_recall_given_resolved` and `retrieval_recall_given_resolved`. **Assert byte-identical across R0–R8**; a change means grouping or resolution leaked into the comparison.
- `D_candidate` — subset of `D_node_bearing` present in the candidate pool. Denominator for `retrieval_recall_given_candidate`.
- `R` for R-Precision / Recall@R = `|D_node_bearing|` for that question. Questions with `R = 0` report `null` and are counted separately — never scored as 0 (this mirrors the existing `expected_recall_evaluability` discipline at `retrieval_v2.py:4`).

**Composites:** one unit in every denominator (components never enter the unique-target inventory separately). `RETRIEVED` iff *all* node-bearing components appear in top-k. A separate `composite_partial_credit` fraction is reported as a diagnostic and never enters headline recall. COMPOSITE is excluded from `canonical_resolution_coverage`.

**Evidence-backed:** in `D_representable` and `D_all`; excluded from `D_node_bearing`; outcome always `UNREPRESENTABLE` for entity retrieval, reported as such rather than deleted.

**Type-B source retrieval:** denominator = required sources that resolve to an article node in the snapshot (extends `source_mapping_coverage`, `retrieval_v2.py:46`). Report `source_recall@k` = distinct resolved required-source articles in the provenance union of the top-k evidence ÷ resolved required sources; plus `source_hit@k`; plus `source_recall_lower_bound` over all required citations including unresolvable ones. Also emit `articles_touched` per question — otherwise a larger k silently inflates the provenance union and `source_recall@k` rises for free.

---

## 5. Edge cases to handle explicitly

Empty field (no claims/tasks) — must contribute a neutral, *documented* score, not 0 and not a KeyError; the choice biases short-context nodes either way, so state it. · `year`/`origin_year` absent after snapshot filtering (R-j). · Groups spanning multiple types — `member_types` is a list; type priors must aggregate (recommend max over members, documented). · A group containing two *different* gold targets → this is a grouping bug; assert and fail loudly rather than silently merging. · Composite where one component resolves and another does not. · Ambiguous resolution must not be silently promoted when only one candidate survives snapshot filtering. · `k > |candidates|`. · Zero-norm field vectors (`normalize` at `retrieval.py:5` already clamps; keep it). · The 2026 cutoff run — resolution and grouping must be recomputed per snapshot, not reused from 2025. · Question with no extractive views (E2 yields nothing) → fall back to the original query and record the fallback.

---

## 6. Validation steps

1. `pytest` green, including `test_v2.py::test_real_type_a_denominator_keeps_all_csv_questions`, which pins 14 Type-A / 12 evaluable / `{Q5,Q11}` against `artifacts/evaluation/target_mapping_2025.json`. **That file must not change**, or the existing v2 path has been perturbed.
2. Re-run `evaluate-v2` and diff `artifacts/evaluation/extrinsic_v2.json` against the pre-change copy — byte-identical except for `protocol.code_hashes`. This is the hard preservation check.
3. Assert `D_node_bearing` identical across all ablation rows.
4. Assert the gold entity-group count identical in R1 and R2.
5. Embedding-normalization test over query, name, field, centroid, and prototype vectors (S14).
6. Sanity gate from the request: on the questions where nearly all labels have literal graph matches, `present_in_flat_candidates` must be true for essentially all of them once routing is a prior — if not, the bug is eligibility, and no amount of context will help.
7. Determinism: run each ablation twice, assert identical ranked IDs (the existing `test_prototypes_can_expose_diluted_branch` pattern).
8. Temporal leakage test: a 2026 node must never appear in a 2025 run's candidates or context fields.
9. Tests S1–S24 on **synthetic** graphs only.

---

## 7. Assumptions and open questions

**Assumptions I have made:** `members[0]` is the subject of a hyperedge (unverified — measure it, R-f); node `surface_form` is the only text a node carries (confirmed: no description field); the 12/40/120 hierarchy has a singleton finest level, so leaves exist and the zero recall is *not* a missing-leaf bug (`hierarchy.py:54` enforces this); the BGE query prefix is acceptable as a benchmark-independent fix.

**Questions for you before Codex commits to a design:**

1. **Is the BGE query prefix in scope?** It is not "threshold tuning" and needs no new model, but it changes every v2-comparable number. My recommendation: yes, as its own row R0b. Confirm.
2. **Composite scoring rule** — I propose all-components-required with separate partial-credit reporting. The alternative (any-component) inflates recall. Confirm the strict rule.
3. **Does `artifacts/baseline_v1/manifest.json` list any `src/**` paths?** If yes, `verify_reuse` breaks the moment a module is added and needs a decision (R-k).
4. **`k` semantics under grouping** — is top-10 *groups* an acceptable comparison against top-10 *nodes*, or do you want an equal-node-budget variant as the primary R2 row?
5. **Multi-query cost** — should R4 be compared at equal `vectors_scored` (fewer entities per view) or at equal entity coverage (3–5× the cost)? This determines whether R4 can ever look favourable on the cost axis.
6. Where the generic-head-noun DF percentile (R-e) should be fixed — I suggest top-1% by document frequency over node surface forms, declared in config and computed from the graph alone.
